Emily — thanks for the redlines and for flagging the objection window. Quick answers up front:
- Our standard notification is to provide the updated subprocessor list 30 days before onboarding, with an objection window of 15 business days from notice receipt.
- We routinely execute via DocuSign; we can accept AdobeSign in specific cases but prefer DocuSign for envelope tracking.

I've attached the tracked DPA (Redwood_DPA_v3_track-changes.pdf) with comments on the data transfer and liability sections. Laura (cc'd) is Redwood's contracting counsel and will confirm whether we can compress the objection period.

I'll also attach the current subprocessor CSV in a follow-up email to avoid large attachments in the same message.

Next steps: Laura to confirm legal position on the 10-day request, David to coordinate the commercial side if any concession is required, and I can prepare the DocuSign envelope once legal is aligned.

Hi Emily — following up from Vanessa. I reviewed the redlines; the main change you propose (10-business-day objection) is aggressive from a programmatic standpoint. Our standard 15-business-day window balances customer review time with the operational scheduling of pipeline onboarding and the right to maintain security confidence.

Two options we can offer:
1) Accept 15 business days and provide a curated threat-profile export for any new subprocessor so SafeShip's security team can prioritize review.
2) Keep 30-day notice but allow SafeShip to request expedited review (10 business days) on a case-by-case basis for critical subprocessors; Redwood will prioritize if the request is made in writing.

Regarding e-signature: we can execute via AdobeSign with one small admin step (mapping the signature fields) but our standard envelope automation uses DocuSign. If Procurement insists on AdobeSign, we can accommodate — it'll just add a 24–48 hour processing window.

Let me know which option fits SafeShip's process.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com

Laura — thanks. SafeShip's security team prefers the 10-business-day baseline for objection so they can complete vendor risk scoring quickly; however, we can take option (1) if necessary. Two asks before we can sign:
1) Please send the current subprocessor list CSV (we need hostnames and country of processing columns)
2) Confirm in the DPA that, for EU transfers, Redwood will use SCCs + documented technical safeguards (we've highlighted this in our redlines).

If you can supply the CSV and a short confirmation on SCCs, Procurement will prepare the PO and we can finalize the e-sign.

Emily
